walkthroughs.body_html:
On 17 November 1558 Elizabeth I succeeded her half-sister Mary I.

She inherited debt, a divided Church and threats from France and Spain. She was 25, unmarried and Protestant. Her chief minister William Cecil ran daily government from 1558.

Parliament passed two laws in 1559.

The Act of Supremacy made Elizabeth Supreme Governor — not Head — of the Church. The Act of Uniformity set an English Book of Common Prayer and a 1s fine for not attending church.

Elizabeth rewarded loyal nobles like Cecil, Robert Dudley and Francis Walsingham.

She balanced rival factions and used progresses across the country to bond with subjects. Her unmarried image — the 'Virgin Queen' — became a powerful tool of propaganda.

mcqs.q: What was the Elizabethan Religious Settlement of 1559?
options: Elizabeth I personally commanded the English fleet at sea.
A deliberate via media — a Protestant doctrine and English-language prayer book combined with some Catholic-style ceremony — designed to maximise conformity.
Elizabeth reunited England with the Pope to make peace with Spain.
Elizabeth made England fully Protestant and banned Catholic worship outright.

mcqs.q: Why was the Spanish Armada defeated in 1588?
options: Elizabeth reunited England with the Pope to make peace with Spain.
A combination of English tactics and fireships, poor Spanish planning, and the 'Protestant wind' storms that wrecked the fleet on the return.
Drake defeated the Armada single-handedly in a great sea battle.
Elizabeth I personally commanded the English fleet at sea.

mcqs.q: Did the New Deal end the Great Depression?
options: It eased unemployment and restored confidence but did not end the Depression — WWII spending did. Roosevelt's reforms reshaped American government permanently.
The New Deal was a treaty with Britain to share gold reserves.
Roosevelt's New Deal ended the Great Depression by 1936.
